# HTML Prerender

> Improve SEO for single-page applications

HTML Prerender improves search engine optimization and social media link previews for single-page applications by serving fully rendered HTML to bots and crawlers.

Modern JavaScript frameworks like React, Vue, Angular, Blazor, and others make building rich, interactive experiences easier. However, search engines and AI crawlers don't execute JavaScript during indexing, which means your content can be missed or deprioritized.

HTML Prerender solves this by capturing fully rendered HTML snapshots and serving them to bots, while your users continue to receive the full dynamic application.

## How to enable

1. Open your Pull Zone settings
2. Navigate to Optimizer
3. Enable Bunny Optimizer if not already enabled
4. Enable HTML Prerender

Changes propagate across the CDN within a few minutes. Crawlers and bots will immediately start receiving fully rendered HTML snapshots.

# Edge Pre-rendering

Crawled generates and caches rendered HTML snapshots of your public pages, then serves those snapshots to recognised search engines and AI crawlers from the edge. Normal users continue to experience the original website.

## The pre-rendering edge function

Crawled's pre-rendering edge function detects recognised crawler requests, checks for a cached HTML snapshot of the requested page, and serves the pre-rendered version from the edge. Where no snapshot exists, Crawled can generate or request one, cache it, and return crawler-readable HTML.

Same content, two delivery paths.

Crawled is not designed to show different content to crawlers and users. The pre-rendered snapshot should represent the same public content available to users.

## How a request flows

1. Request hits the edge - The pre-rendering edge function inspects the User-Agent.
2. Recognised crawler? - If yes, Crawled looks up a cached HTML snapshot for that URL.
3. Cache hit - The pre-rendered snapshot is returned immediately.
4. Cache miss - Crawled generates a snapshot, caches it for 24 hours, and returns it. Subsequent crawler requests for the same URL are served from cache and don't count against your quota.
